subject: general
question:
Match the column (shortcuts & functions).

 
 

 1. Alt + Shift + N
 I. Mark index entry.
 
 

 2. Alt + Shift + I
 II. Insert Page field with current Page.
 
 

 3. Alt + Shift + O
 III. Mark citation.
 
 

 4. Alt + Shift + X
 IV. Mail Merge to a new document.
 
 

 5. Alt + Shift + P
 V. Mark Table of Contents.
solution:
the correct answer is __**1.IV 2.III 3.V 4. I 5.**II__

__
 
• **Mark index entry, Mark citation, Mark table of Contents** are the tools of **Reference Tab**.
 
• **Mail merge to a New document** is **the tool of Mailings Tab.**

 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__** 

__**Description of Each tool**__

**1. Mark the Index entries**

__
 
• **An index list is the terms and topics** that are discussed i**n a document, along with the pages that they appear on.**
 
• To create an **index, mark the index entries** by providing the name of the main entry and the cross-reference in your document, and then you build the index.
 
• We can create an index entry for an **individual word, phrase, or symbol.**
 
• **Alt + Shift + X** is the shortcut of this tool.

**Steps to add and create an Index**__

__
 
• **Step 1**: Select the text to use as **an index entry**, or just click where we want to insert the entry.
 
• **Step 2**: On **the References tab**, in **the Index group**, click **Mark Entry**.

 [IMAGE: https://support.content.office.net/en-us/media/c9e344c3-6214-4465-959b-9673228eada4.png] 

 
• **Step 3**:We can edit the text in **the Mark Index Entry dialog box.**

 
 
• We can add a second-level in the Subentry box. If we need a third level, follow the subentry text with a colon.
 
• To create a cross-reference to another entry, click Cross-reference under Options, and then type the text for the other entry in the box.
 
• To format the page numbers that will appear in the index, select the Bold check box or Italic check box below Page number format.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://support.content.office.net/en-us/media/ac874a0d-caa0-4731-a300-50a264a69761.png] 

 
• **Step 4**: Click Mark to mark the index entry. To mark this text everywhere it shows up in the document, **click Mark All**.
 
• **Step 5**:To mark **additional index entries,** select the text, click in the **Mark Index Entry dialog box**, and then **repeat steps 3 and 4.**

**2. Mark Citation**

 
• In Word, we can easily **add citations** when writing a document where you need to cite your sources, such as a research paper.
 
• Citations can be added in various formats, **including APA, Chicago-style, and MLA.**
 
• Afterward, we can create **a bibliography of the sources you used to write our paper.**
 
• To add a citation to your document, we first **add the source that we used.**
 
• **Alt + Shift + I** is the short cut of this tool.

 

Creating a New Citation Source & Inserting it in a Document__

 
 

 Steps
 Description
 Images
 
 

 1 
 Place the cursor where we want the citation to be inserted.
 
 
 

 2
 In the Citations & Bibliography group, click the arrow located on the Insert Citation button.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b19d80d307db3198835dd3019f81e40e1d619403cf4af4a15de7d8432e068df.png] 
 
 

 4
 Click Add New Source
 
 
 

 5
 In the dialog box that will pop‐up, from the Type of Source list, select the type of citation and then fill in the required fields. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/79d6707cf703de67df968cb71f3b7210a5ea82b4a52707e661d68d36cf5883ef.png] 
 
 

 6
 Click ok after done.
 
 
 

 

**3. Table of Contents**

 
• **Table of Contents **- Drop-Down. Provide an overview of your document by adding a table of contents.

 
 
• The drop-down contains the commands: Built-in, Insert Table of Contents, and Save Selection to Table of Contents Gallery.
 
 
 
• **Add Text** - The drop-down contains the commands: Do Not Show in Table of Contents, Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3.
 
• **Update Table **- Updates the table of contents so that all the entries refer to the correct page numbers.
 
• **Alt + Shift + O** is the shortcut for this tool.

 

**4. Start Mail Merge Group**

 
• This group is used to start the Mail Merge process
 
• It is a powerful tool for writing a personalized letter or e-mail to many people at the same time.
 
• It imports data from another source and then uses that to replace placeholders throughout the message with the relevant information for each individual that is being messaged.
 
• **Alt + Shift + N** is the shortcut for this tool.​

 
 

 Tools
 Description
 
 

 Start Mail Merge
 
 
 
• Use this button to select the type of document that is to be created such as letters, e-mail messages, envelopes, labels, and a directory.
 
• When envelopes or labels are selected, a dialog box will display which allows for the selection of the size envelopes or labels that are to be used for the merge.
 
• This button is also used to access the Step-by-Step Mail Merge Wizard.
 
• This wizard provides step-by-step instructions for creating the Mail Merge.
 
 
 
 

 Select Recipients
 
 
 
• This button is used to select a list of recipients that was created earlier either in Excel or Access.
 
• It is also used when a new list of recipients needs to be created.
 
• The new list will be created using an Access database.
 
 
 
 

 Edit Recipient List 
 
 
 
• Use this button to make changes to the list of recipients or to decide which recipients are to receive the letter.
 
• Sorting and filtering options are available in this area.
